$comment: Evidence retention, per bucket prefix. Applied with `npm run evidence:retention` and read back
from the store itself, so the policy that is enforced and the policy that is documented are the
Why it is per prefix: PROJECT.md P3 records the actual estate problem — 'some systems storing
footage for 7 days and others for 15 days or more'. A single global number would model an
estate that does not exist. The key convention evidence/<camera_id>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/... is what
makes a department's own clock expressible as a prefix rule.
Rules are evaluated by S3 with the LONGEST matching prefix winning, so the catch-all sits first
here for readability only; order in this file has no effect.
These are OUR crops, not the departments' video. We store no footage — a crop is a few KB of a
single frame. The clock still matters: an alert whose crop has expired is an alert nobody can
verify, and D3-05 surfaces exactly that.

rules.note: Catch-all. 15 days matches the longer of the two retention regimes the challenge brief describes, so our evidence never expires before the source footage it points at.
A watchlist hit is the crop an investigation is built on. D3-04's export bundles hash these bytes, so a 15-day clock would break a manifest three weeks after it was signed.
